Interviewer:	I have just got a few questions then about how the placement’s going and how you think it relates to the course you are doing. So when did you start the placement?

Subject:	I started my placement on 5 July 2004.

Interviewer:	Ok, so you have nearly finished it now then? 

Subject:	Yes

Interviewer:	Ok. Can you tell me a bit about the company that you are working for and what they do?

Subject:	I’m working for [company] group, yes it’s a construction company, a construction company.

Interviewer:	How useful do you think that your course has been so far to the work that you are doing on placement?

Subject:	Oh, erm for my course let me see. Well I have got to do things I’ve studied in theory, I’ve done them in practical. Yes

Interviewer:	Is there any particular skill that you think has been useful?

Subject:	Well yes, my measurement skills. I have got to know more about design and what is involved in it. I have also got to know about the structure in construction and what is involved in it.

Interviewer:	Ok. Is there anything that you wish you had learnt before you started placement?

Subject:	Well I would have loved to like learn more like let me see more measurement like to do (Yes) More measurement at university.

Interviewer:	Ok, were you taught anything about health and safety at university?

Subject:	Yes I was.

Interviewer:	Has that been useful on your placement?

Subject:	Yes it has.

Interviewer:	Yes, have you had to do a lot of health and safety training on placement?

Subject:	I had to go through an induction for my first week and erm I also went on a health and safety course.

Interviewer:	Ok. How did you find that?

Subject:	It was good.

Interviewer:	Ok. How have you found the transition from education to work? Was it easy or difficult?

Subject:	In the beginning it was exciting, but it was also difficult getting used to the system. At the moment, I’m enjoying it.

Interviewer:	Ok. What sorts of things were difficult?

Subject:	At the moment, like I’m waking up at 8 o’clock and being at work by 8 o’clock and then erm going through a whole day like the system for a number of hours, going through the whole day. But I mean you get used to it in time.

Interviewer:	It’s just different from being at university.

Subject:	Yes.

Interviewer:	Ok, do you feel like you have had to face any new issues at all like office politics or dealing with different people like the boss or customers or anything like that?

Subject:	At the moment, the site I’m working on, the people have been very good to me and all that, but sometimes its hard to get some things considering you are a placement student, getting work like for example like getting something like essentials like maybe getting a computer, there are like ‘hold on you’re a placement student you don’t need this and that this time’ and all that. (Yes) I mean there’s so much bureaucracy to get some things.

Interviewer:	Yes. Have you found that quite frustrating?

Subject:	Yes it has been frustrating.

Interviewer:	Ok. What do you think are the main differences between being at work and being at university?

Subject:	Erm, well being at work most of the time is taken like because you do Monday to Friday to a certain system, which I mean if you don’t want - when you are at university you plan your own time and you do your own thing. (Yes) You attend your lectures but I mean lectures are just about one hour (Yes) which is not bad.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that university and work have different priorities and goals?

Subject:	Well I mean in university you’re gaining knowledge, while you’re at work, ok, there’s knowledge you need, but at the end of the day the employer wants you to do something that will benefit the company.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. How do you feel about going back to university when you have finished the placement? Are you looking forward to it?

Subject:	Erm, yes I am actually. In November, I mean apart from earning the money (Yes) well when I will be going back it will be in September, so hopefully I will have prepared enough to get ready for university.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do [company] employ many women?

Subject:	At the moment, I only know of 2 surveyors who are women for [company] but I haven’t seen very many women about here. 

Interviewer:	OK. How would you describe the company’s attitude to women?

Subject:	Well at the moment, they are trying to encourage more women into the construction industry. (Yes) Which is pretty good really. I mean they don’t treat you any different from the males.

Interviewer:	Ok. That’s good. Have you had a programme to follow or a structure in place for being a placement student with targets or anything like that?

Subject:	Well at the moment, my boss has helped me go through it when I got onto site. I had this diary where I had to record certain things and then sometimes it also involved what you wanted yourself, so I sat down and I thought maybe by the end of this placement I want to have learnt this and this, measurement (advancement?), procurement and (so many things I want to learn?) in the construction industry. Well I mean in general it’s up to you to push it really. I mean the training department tells you all these instructions and that but when you get onto the site, you’re alone and you have to push it and you just do it in your own way. 

Interviewer:	Ok. Would you like more support on that then?

Subject:	Yes I would like more support on that. Like whereby you know they encourage you to go on more courses. We did go on some courses but I mean more for your study purposes than you know

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. What does your job in the company actually involve?

Subject:	At the moment? (Yes) What I’m doing is more of, I’m working on a (PS5?) school in London and I’m working, I’m an assistant QS, so I help the main QS who’s working on this job, in doing the measurements, the procurement and the sort of evaluation of sub contractors, mainly managing sub contractors.

Interviewer:	Ok. Have you been working on that project all the time?

Subject:	Yes I have

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you feel like you have been given an appropriate level of responsibility?

Subject:	Yes I have, yes.

Interviewer:	Not too much or too little?

Subject:	Well sometimes it’s too little and sometimes it’s too much, but it balances out.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you feel like the people that you are working with are supportive in?

Subject:	Yes they are supportive.

Interviewer:	Can you say to them whether you want more responsibility or less responsibility?

Subject:	I can tell them that I want more responsibility (and that’s useful really), because we did an evaluation of my work that I had done after 6 months. (Yes) I said I want more responsibility and I’d like to get involved in this and that.

Interviewer:	Ok. And they were supportive of you doing that? Ok. How would you summarise the placement so far then?

Subject:	Oh the placement has been good so far really and it has given me the experiences that I expected to get.

Interviewer:	Ok, so it’s met your expectations? Ok. What would you say has been the best and worse things about the placement so far?

Subject:	Well I mean the placement, let me see the best thing is to put in practice what you learn at university, you get to realise that this is what it is all about, and then the worst thing is (Inaudible) you don’t know what to expect so it would be much better if they give you more guidance and tell you oh this is how the structure is supposed to be and go to this training and all that and that.

Interviewer:	Would that be from the company or from the university?

Subject:	The company (Ok) But it would also be good if the university would be, something saying oh ‘this is what we expect students to learn from a placement’ you know, because sometime you end up pushy and trying to get something you know, the company would just keep quiet and you don’t get to do what you are supposed to be doing.

Interviewer:	Yes, Ok. Do you think that there are any drawbacks to doing a placement or is it all positive things? 

Subject:	Erm. Well the drawbacks in cases whereby you not erm doing what you are supposed to doing like for example if you just, I mean for almost 6 months you know improving on what you are doing, for example like, you’re not learning what you did at university.
Interviewer:	Yes, yes. But that hasn’t been your experience? OK. Do you think you have changed personally as a result of the placement, like more confident or independent things like that?

Subject:	Yes I have become more confident, more independent. Learn to make more decisions on my own. 

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. You said you are using what you have learnt at university and putting it into practice now, do you think that you will use what you are learning now when you come back to university for your final year?

Subject:	Yes definitely.

Interviewer:	OK. What sort of things do you think you will maybe use?

Subject:	Well first of all like basic skills like time management really. And what else, for example, learning about construction technology, I’ll be able to know what exactly he is talking about, is he talking about simple structures and all that. I will be able use my practical side to be able to understand what he is talking about.

Interviewer:	Ok. Are there any other students on placement with you?

Subject:	Erm no.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that you are treated the same as permanent members of staff.

Subject:	Yes in a way but not that much really.

Interviewer:	Ok. Is that the things like not getting computers and stuff like that?

Subject:	Yes

Interviewer:	Ok. Does your work involve a lot of team work

Subject:	Oh yes it does. A lot of team work.

Interviewer:	Ok. How do you think that doing the group work in the work place compares to doing group work at university.

Subject:	Erm, I mean with the university it’s a bit, I mean it’s the same thing really because you don’t know who you are working with, and you get two, three people and you get to work with them. I mean it teaches you how to get to start working with other people and getting to know them. (Yes) Passing on interest for the company for you to get along because you have to do your job and if you don’t get along with people I mean you won’t be able to do your job properly.

Interviewer:	Ok. Have you found it easier doing team work at work or at university?

Subject:	Yes, I am far better at doing team work here than at university. I don’t know, because may this team I’m working with is very good, but. At university people either don’t care, you can get in a team of people who don’t really want to do their work and end up doing the right thing but then at work people tend to do their work and get it done.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. Are there any particular people that you have liked or disliked working with?

Subject:	Erm, no not really.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that doing group work at university prepares you for doing group work in the workplace?

Subject:	No not so much. (Ok) It doesn’t do that much. I don’t think so.

Interviewer:	Do you think that it is worth doing the group work at university then or would you rather do individual work at university?

Subject:	I’d rather do individual work at university

Interviewer:	Why do you think that is?

Subject:	Well I mean, I don’t know, maybe because people when they take in uni life very easy going and not, they don’t take their work very serious. Sometimes you know that could damage your career, if you are working with people who have such an attitude. (Yes) Yes. Work I tend to I don’t know, whether people who are working really want to get the job done, so you end up you know working with people who are motivated to doing what they want to do

Interviewer:	OK, that’s great. Have you got a mentor at all in the company?

Subject:	Erm, well at the moment I’m kind of my boss, the person I’m working for is acting like my mentor at the moment.

Interviewer:	Yes. What do you think being a mentor involves?

Subject:	Well erm giving you guidance with your work and then being able to help you through your training and teaching you a lot about your career path.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. So do you think that the person you think of as your mentor has been a good mentor then?

Subject:	Yes, he has been a good mentor.

Interviewer:	What sort of advice has he been giving you about things like career and stuff?

Subject:	Well he’s given me advice about my APC [Assessment of Professional Competence] training and he’s been able to help to go through it like whenever I have problems. I go to him and ask him ‘what’s this supposed to be’ and ‘what does this mean’ and he’s able to help me do that. And also when I’m having difficulty understanding stuff on daily work, he can help me.

Interviewer:	Yes. Is there anyone else that you would go to for advice at all?

Subject:	Erm, I have got a very good relationship with the people whom I’m working with on site I have been able to ask people working with me about different things.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. Is there anyone in the company that you would regard as a role model at all?

Subject:	Erm. Let’s see erm well I mean. Because most of them, the people I’m working with are determined to do the job and I’m kind of like motivated and doing a good job and doing the best. So I mean there are quite a few of the engineers that are like role models because they make their work enjoyable and look nice and also my boss, he works hard, extremely hard. (Yes) So I have ended up you know taking up different role models.

Interviewer:	Different characteristics from different people

Subject:	Yes

Interviewer:	Has anyone from university been to visit you yet?

Subject:	Yes I invited one of the lecturers to come over and look at me and see what I was doing.

Interviewer:	Yes. Did you know the person that came to visit you already? Had they taught you the person that …

Subject:	No I actually had to call up and try and find out what, it was a bit, you know, not very organised really.

Interviewer:	Ok. Would you rather someone different came to visit you.

Subject:	No, no, no I liked the person that came to visit me but all I’m saying is the university wasn’t able to say ‘this is the person that is coming to see you’

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok.

Subject:	I had to you know like call up and see who is the person, and all that

Interviewer:	Ok. So do you think that could have been better organised?

Subject:	Yes, better organised.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. What sort of things did the lecturer talk to you about?

Subject:	Oh well he went through, he asked me what sub contractors I was managing, went through all that and then he talked about my APC training and what I was planning to do about my dissertation.

Interviewer:	Ok. Did they talk to your manager as well?

Subject:	Yes, they did.

Interviewer:	Ok. Would you be happy to go to this person if you did have any problems on placement?

Subject:	Erm, well I mean, I don’t really know the influence he would be able to have to change whatever I’m facing at work, all the problems of working. So it would be a bit difficult for me to go and ask him.

Interviewer:	Ok. Would you go to someone else at university if you had problems then or would you try and sort it within the company?

Subject:	I would have to solve it myself really.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you know if either university or the workplace has a complaints procedure to follow if you did have any problems?

Subject:	Yes, I mean because I was told at the beginning of my job, I think I must have been told. Well they said whatever happens it will be good. For my work, they were like if you are having problems you have to first go to the person you are in directly in contact with, then if that fails you go to the next person. And if it does fail or there is a serious problem you go to the director.

Interviewer:	Do you think it’s a good idea that you were told about that before anything happened so if something?

Subject:	Yes it’s a good idea.

Interviewer:	I have just got a couple of questions now about being a woman and things like that. Do you think that there are appropriate facilities for women on the site that you are working at?

Subject:	Nope. Well, I’d prefer having my own toilet I think

Interviewer:	So there aren’t women’s toilets?

Subject:	No 

Interviewer:	Ok. What about safety clothing and stuff like that? Does that fit or is it all in big men’s sizes?

Subject:	Big Men’s sizes. You have to wait 4 months waiting for your size.

Interviewer:	Ok. How do you feel about that? Has that been frustrating or?

Subject:	Frustrating really in the beginning because you couldn’t go on the site because you don’t have safety boots. (Yes) Yes, you had to wait.

Interviewer:	You had to wait, did you have to wait 4 months before you could go on site

Subject:	It was about 2 weeks really.

Interviewer:	Ok. Can you think of any occasions where you feel like the fact that you are a woman has determined reactions that you have got from people at all?

Subject:	Yes sometimes you know, I mean they tend to keep quiet about it really. Yes. And they don’t say anything (Ok) Well you see it in their eyes and they say oh

Interviewer:	Like act surprised

Subject:	Act surprised. But they don’t like tell you directly you are a woman.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. How does that make you feel? 

Subject:	Erm well you just ignore it really and you just get mad about it but in the end you just keep quiet about it.

Interviewer:	Do you still want a career in the engineering industry?

Subject:	Yes. I mean I’m doing quantity surveying really but I would like quantity surveying but after I finish QSing, working in a consultancy.

Interviewer:	Ok. So do you think that you would like a more managerial or a more technical role?

Subject:	I think I would like a more managerial role.

Interviewer:	Do you think that doing the placement has changed your career ambitions at all?

Subject:	No not really. I mean it’s made me more motivated to do what I really want to do and get it done. 

Interviewer:	Yes, so it has reinforced your ideas. Ok. Do you think that the placement will help you when you start work after you have finished university?

Subject:	Yes, I hope it will help me because I’ve got a year and a half’s experience so far which will be a very good thing on my CV.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that the placement experience will help you cope when you start work after graduation? 

Subject:	Well I will know what to expect when I’ve graduated, it will have helped me a lot.

Interviewer:	Ok. I have just got one more question. Would you like to work for [company] when you graduate if you had the opportunity?

Subject:	Yes, I would like to.

Interviewer:	Do you know whether you would be able to or not? 

Subject:	Oh well at the moment everyone says I’ll be working with them. So I just have to re-apply and at the moment I’m asking for sponsorship for my final year.

Interviewer:	Ok. Now I have just got a last few questions and they are questions that I asked you in the first interview, not to test you but to see whether your opinion has changed as a result of doing the placement. The first question is probably the hardest and that’s what 5 words would you use to describe your field of engineering or the characteristics of your field of engineering?

Subject:	Erm, it’s (inaudible) driven at times, it’s highly commercial, yes and erm it’s trying to improve health and safety and erm you know especially if you are a contractor you have to be on site more often, it’s more like a wall like a dirty wall you have to be there (inaudible) and erm sometimes it’s good fun.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that there are advantages or disadvantages to being a woman in engineering?

Subject:	Erm, I mean the advantages at the moment are they are trying to encourage more women in the industry to get a job and then the advantages the women I get they are more commercially aware of things so in a QS role that would be very important. (Yes) Then erm, disadvantages you know like the outfits, 90% just don’t care what you look like on site and then the facilities sometimes, I mean like having your own toilet and those kind of things are a disadvantage.

Interviewer:	Ok. Does it concern you at all that there are so few women in engineering?

Subject:	Yes it does concern me. Because I mean when you want to have a girl’s night out you don’t have anyone to, you know you’re usually going out with the guys all the time. (Yes) But once in a while you’d like to hang out with a female or something like that, and on this site I’m the only female.

Interviewer:	Ok. Do you think that more women should be encouraged into the industry then?

Subject:	Yes, more women should be encouraged into the industry

Interviewer:	Do you think that more women will come into the industry in the future or do you think it will stay the same?

Subject:	I think it’s going to stay the same.

Interviewer:	Why do you think that is?

Subject:	It is the (law?), I mean the way people describe construction, well it’s the honest truth really, and how it is you know and some women prefer an office.

Interviewer:	Yes. Ok. Do you think the construction industry can do anything to encourage more women into the industry?

Subject:	Erm, erm I mean at the moment they are in doing their best to encourage women really maybe into health and safety places and I suppose improve the facilities for women and that’s it really.

Interviewer:	Yes. OK, that’s everything, thank you very much. I hope that the rest of the placement goes well.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well I mean the placement, let me see the best thing is to put in practice what you learn at university, you get to realise that this is what it is all about, and then the worst thing is (Inaudible) you don’t know what to expect so it would be much better if they give you more guidance and tell you oh this is how the structure is supposed to be and go to this training and all that and that.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Would that be from the company or from the university?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: The company (Ok) But it would also be good if the university would be, something saying oh ‘this is what we expect students to learn from a placement’ you know, because sometime you end up pushy and trying to get something you know, the company would just keep quiet and you don’t get to do what you are supposed to be doing.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes, Ok. Do you think that there are any drawbacks to doing a placement or is it all positive things?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm. Well the drawbacks in cases whereby you not erm doing what you are supposed to doing like for example if you just, I mean for almost 6 months you know improving on what you are doing, for example like, you’re not learning what you did at university.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes, yes. But that hasn’t been your experience? OK. Do you think you have changed personally as a result of the placement, like more confident or independent things like that?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes I have become more confident, more independent. Learn to make more decisions on my own.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. You said you are using what you have learnt at university and putting it into practice now, do you think that you will use what you are learning now when you come back to university for your final year?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes definitely.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK. What sort of things do you think you will maybe use?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well first of all like basic skills like time management really. And what else, for example, learning about construction technology, I’ll be able to know what exactly he is talking about, is he talking about simple structures and all that. I will be able use my practical side to be able to understand what he is talking about.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Are there any other students on placement with you?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm no.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you think that you are treated the same as permanent members of staff.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes in a way but not that much really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Is that the things like not getting computers and stuff like that?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Does your work involve a lot of team work

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Oh yes it does. A lot of team work.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. How do you think that doing the group work in the work place compares to doing group work at university.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, I mean with the university it’s a bit, I mean it’s the same thing really because you don’t know who you are working with, and you get two, three people and you get to work with them. I mean it teaches you how to get to start working with other people and getting to know them. (Yes) Passing on interest for the company for you to get along because you have to do your job and if you don’t get along with people I mean you won’t be able to do your job properly.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Have you found it easier doing team work at work or at university?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, I am far better at doing team work here than at university. I don’t know, because may this team I’m working with is very good, but. At university people either don’t care, you can get in a team of people who don’t really want to do their work and end up doing the right thing but then at work people tend to do their work and get it done.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. Are there any particular people that you have liked or disliked working with?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, no not really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you think that doing group work at university prepares you for doing group work in the workplace?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No not so much. (Ok) It doesn’t do that much. I don’t think so.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that it is worth doing the group work at university then or would you rather do individual work at university?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I’d rather do individual work at university

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Why do you think that is?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well I mean, I don’t know, maybe because people when they take in uni life very easy going and not, they don’t take their work very serious. Sometimes you know that could damage your career, if you are working with people who have such an attitude. (Yes) Yes. Work I tend to I don’t know, whether people who are working really want to get the job done, so you end up you know working with people who are motivated to doing what they want to do

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: OK, that’s great. Have you got a mentor at all in the company?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, well at the moment I’m kind of my boss, the person I’m working for is acting like my mentor at the moment.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. What do you think being a mentor involves?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well erm giving you guidance with your work and then being able to help you through your training and teaching you a lot about your career path.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. So do you think that the person you think of as your mentor has been a good mentor then?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, he has been a good mentor.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: What sort of advice has he been giving you about things like career and stuff?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well he’s given me advice about my APC [Assessment of Professional Competence] training and he’s been able to help to go through it like whenever I have problems. I go to him and ask him ‘what’s this supposed to be’ and ‘what does this mean’ and he’s able to help me do that. And also when I’m having difficulty understanding stuff on daily work, he can help me.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Is there anyone else that you would go to for advice at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, I have got a very good relationship with the people whom I’m working with on site I have been able to ask people working with me about different things.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. Is there anyone in the company that you would regard as a role model at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm. Let’s see erm well I mean. Because most of them, the people I’m working with are determined to do the job and I’m kind of like motivated and doing a good job and doing the best. So I mean there are quite a few of the engineers that are like role models because they make their work enjoyable and look nice and also my boss, he works hard, extremely hard. (Yes) So I have ended up you know taking up different role models.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Different characteristics from different people

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Has anyone from university been to visit you yet?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes I invited one of the lecturers to come over and look at me and see what I was doing.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Did you know the person that came to visit you already? Had they taught you the person that …

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No I actually had to call up and try and find out what, it was a bit, you know, not very organised really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Would you rather someone different came to visit you.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No, no, no I liked the person that came to visit me but all I’m saying is the university wasn’t able to say ‘this is the person that is coming to see you’

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok.

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I had to you know like call up and see who is the person, and all that

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. So do you think that could have been better organised?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, better organised.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. What sort of things did the lecturer talk to you about?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Oh well he went through, he asked me what sub contractors I was managing, went through all that and then he talked about my APC training and what I was planning to do about my dissertation.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Did they talk to your manager as well?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, they did.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Would you be happy to go to this person if you did have any problems on placement?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, well I mean, I don’t really know the influence he would be able to have to change whatever I’m facing at work, all the problems of working. So it would be a bit difficult for me to go and ask him.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Would you go to someone else at university if you had problems then or would you try and sort it within the company?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I would have to solve it myself really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you know if either university or the workplace has a complaints procedure to follow if you did have any problems?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, I mean because I was told at the beginning of my job, I think I must have been told. Well they said whatever happens it will be good. For my work, they were like if you are having problems you have to first go to the person you are in directly in contact with, then if that fails you go to the next person. And if it does fail or there is a serious problem you go to the director.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think it’s a good idea that you were told about that before anything happened so if something?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes it’s a good idea.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: I have just got a couple of questions now about being a woman and things like that. Do you think that there are appropriate facilities for women on the site that you are working at?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Nope. Well, I’d prefer having my own toilet I think

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: So there aren’t women’s toilets?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. What about safety clothing and stuff like that? Does that fit or is it all in big men’s sizes?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Big Men’s sizes. You have to wait 4 months waiting for your size.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. How do you feel about that? Has that been frustrating or?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Frustrating really in the beginning because you couldn’t go on the site because you don’t have safety boots. (Yes) Yes, you had to wait.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: You had to wait, did you have to wait 4 months before you could go on site

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: It was about 2 weeks really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Can you think of any occasions where you feel like the fact that you are a woman has determined reactions that you have got from people at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes sometimes you know, I mean they tend to keep quiet about it really. Yes. And they don’t say anything (Ok) Well you see it in their eyes and they say oh

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Like act surprised

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Act surprised. But they don’t like tell you directly you are a woman.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. How does that make you feel?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm well you just ignore it really and you just get mad about it but in the end you just keep quiet about it.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you still want a career in the engineering industry?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes. I mean I’m doing quantity surveying really but I would like quantity surveying but after I finish QSing, working in a consultancy.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. So do you think that you would like a more managerial or a more technical role?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think I would like a more managerial role.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that doing the placement has changed your career ambitions at all?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: No not really. I mean it’s made me more motivated to do what I really want to do and get it done.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes, so it has reinforced your ideas. Ok. Do you think that the placement will help you when you start work after you have finished university?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, I hope it will help me because I’ve got a year and a half’s experience so far which will be a very good thing on my CV.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you think that the placement experience will help you cope when you start work after graduation?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Well I will know what to expect when I’ve graduated, it will have helped me a lot.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. I have just got one more question. Would you like to work for [company] when you graduate if you had the opportunity?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, I would like to.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you know whether you would be able to or not?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Oh well at the moment everyone says I’ll be working with them. So I just have to re-apply and at the moment I’m asking for sponsorship for my final year.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Now I have just got a last few questions and they are questions that I asked you in the first interview, not to test you but to see whether your opinion has changed as a result of doing the placement. The first question is probably the hardest and that’s what 5 words would you use to describe your field of engineering or the characteristics of your field of engineering?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, it’s (inaudible) driven at times, it’s highly commercial, yes and erm it’s trying to improve health and safety and erm you know especially if you are a contractor you have to be on site more often, it’s more like a wall like a dirty wall you have to be there (inaudible) and erm sometimes it’s good fun.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you think that there are advantages or disadvantages to being a woman in engineering?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, I mean the advantages at the moment are they are trying to encourage more women in the industry to get a job and then the advantages the women I get they are more commercially aware of things so in a QS role that would be very important. (Yes) Then erm, disadvantages you know like the outfits, 90% just don’t care what you look like on site and then the facilities sometimes, I mean like having your own toilet and those kind of things are a disadvantage.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Does it concern you at all that there are so few women in engineering?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes it does concern me. Because I mean when you want to have a girl’s night out you don’t have anyone to, you know you’re usually going out with the guys all the time. (Yes) But once in a while you’d like to hang out with a female or something like that, and on this site I’m the only female.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Ok. Do you think that more women should be encouraged into the industry then?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Yes, more women should be encouraged into the industry

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Do you think that more women will come into the industry in the future or do you think it will stay the same?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: I think it’s going to stay the same.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Why do you think that is?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: It is the (law?), I mean the way people describe construction, well it’s the honest truth really, and how it is you know and some women prefer an office.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. Ok. Do you think the construction industry can do anything to encourage more women into the industry?

turns.speaker: Subject
turns.text: Erm, erm I mean at the moment they are in doing their best to encourage women really maybe into health and safety places and I suppose improve the facilities for women and that’s it really.

turns.speaker: Interviewer
turns.text: Yes. OK, that’s everything, thank you very much. I hope that the rest of the placement goes well.
